feature_candidates.description: Embedding of tab id, possibly restricted to top-10 tabs with an 'other' bucket, to capture strong tab-level long_view propensity.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Directly exploits tab 4 vs tab 0 gap; likely boosts GAUC because tab is observed at serving time.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Replace raw tab id in model input with learned embedding; include in both BPR and group_softmax models.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None; tab is a contextual feature available at inference.
feature_candidates.name: tab_embedding

feature_candidates.description: Bucket video duration into 0, 1-30, 30-60, >60 seconds and learn an embedding for each bucket.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures non-linear duration effect on long_view; handles zero-duration separately to avoid spurious signals.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Derive from video feature table; add as categorical embedding.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None; duration is static video metadata.
feature_candidates.name: duration_bucket_embedding

feature_candidates.description: User's historical long_view ratio computed from train split only, respecting temporal cutoff before validation.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Adds personalized long_view propensity beyond user static features; could improve within-user ranking.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute in training script from train sequences only; ensure no validation/test labels are used.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Minimal if computed strictly from train and temporal order respected; risk of lookahead if not careful.
feature_candidates.name: user_hist_long_view_ratio

findings.evidence: Tab breakdown in DATA CARD (train) shows large rate differences across tabs.
findings.implication: Since ranking is within user, tab id should be a powerful feature; embedding or one-hot encoding is expected to improve GAUC/nDCG@5.
findings.observation: Train long_view rate varies sharply by tab: tab 4 at 48.93% vs tab 0 at 4.22%, and tab 1 at 38.61%.
findings.title: Tab is a strong within-user discriminator

findings.evidence: DATA CARD lists zero-duration videos and rows; plan hypothesis asserts positive correlation for >60s.
findings.implication: Bucket duration (0, 1-30, 30-60, >60s) to capture non-linear effect and treat zero-duration as a separate category.
findings.observation: 239 videos have zero duration affecting 24,076 train rows; raw duration may mislead since zero is not informative.
findings.title: Video duration needs bucketing due to zero-duration issue

findings.evidence: Plan lists user history hypothesis; DATA CARD shows per-user row distribution enabling such aggregates.
findings.implication: Adding user_hist_long_view_ratio as a history feature may raise within-user ranking, if validated without lookahead.
findings.observation: Per-user past long_view ratio computed from train only can capture individual preference, but must respect temporal order.
findings.title: User history features hold predictive potential but need careful construction

expected_artifacts: Table of train long_view rate by duration bucket and tab (within-user aggregates).
Per-user correlation (ICC) of long_view with tab and duration.
Plot/table of long_view rate by hour-of-day (train).
Summary of user history feature predictive power (e.g., Pearson r with long_view after user-fixed effects).
feature_hypotheses: Video duration (with zero-duration as a special bucket) has positive within-user correlation with long_view, especially >60s.
Tab id 4 (high long-view rate 48.9%) is a strong positive feature even within user.
User's past long_view ratio (computed from train sequences) predicts future long_view beyond static user features.
Time-of-day (hourmin rounded to hour) has weak but additive signal for within-user ranking.
leakage_risks: Do not use video statistics table (full-platform) as it is leaky; if used, caveats required.
Computing user history from entire train+valid could leak future info; use only train, and for validation respect temporal order.
Zero-duration videos (24k rows) must be handled separately to avoid spurious correlations.
Exact duplicate rows (15k) may inflate feature-weight if not deduplicated during analysis.
plan.objective: EDA to identify within-user discriminative features (tab, duration, time, history) that can boost long_view ranking GAUC/nDCG@5 without leakage.
questions: How does long_view rate vary within users by video duration buckets (0, 1-30, 30-60, >60 sec) on train only?
What is the within-user correlation between tab id and long_view, controlling for user fixed effects?
Does hourmin (UTC+8) show a within-user temporal pattern for long_view, e.g., evening vs morning?
What is the discriminative power of user's historical long_view count/ratio (from train) on subsequent long_view?
required_inputs: Train and valid interaction logs (only registered columns).
Train-period user history aggregates (counts of long_view, click, etc.) computed from train split only.

report.recommended_next_focus: Integrate tab embedding and duration bucket features into the baseline; then test user history ratio with strict train-only temporal aggregation.
report.summary: EDA finds tab id and video duration are strong within-user discriminators for long_view; user history features are promising but require strict temporal splitting to avoid leakage.
ui_notes: Display a bar chart of train long_view rate by tab to highlight tab 4 dominance.
Show train long_view rate by duration bucket (0, 1-30, 30-60, >60s) with zero-duration separately.
Note that validation must be temporally disjoint from train history to avoid leakage in user features.
